title: Kant, Hegel and nineteenth-century philosophy
audience: a college student in a philosophy degree program, or an adult studying the same material on their own
purpose: Study Kant's Critique of Pure Reason in depth (the transcendental aesthetic, the deduction of the categories, the analogies of experience and the refutation of idealism), then German idealism (Fichte, Schelling and Hegel), Schopenhauer, Marx's historical materialism, Kierkegaard, Nietzsche, Mill and the pragmatists Peirce and James.
primary_reading: Kant, The Critique of Pure Reason, translated by J. M. D. Meiklejohn (Project Gutenberg, free)

weeks.1: The Critique of Pure Reason: the project of critique
weeks.2: The transcendental aesthetic: space and time
weeks.3: The transcendental deduction of the categories
weeks.4: The analogies of experience: substance and causation
weeks.5: The refutation of idealism and the paralogisms
weeks.6: Transcendental idealism: two-world and two-aspect readings
weeks.8: Hegel: phenomenology, dialectic and the absolute
weeks.9: Schopenhauer: the world as will and representation
weeks.11: Kierkegaard, Nietzsche and the critique of metaphysics
weeks.12: Mill and the pragmatists: Peirce and James

blocks.deliverable: Reconstruct the argument that the representation of space is a priori.
Explain the second analogy's reply to Hume.
Compare the two readings of things in themselves.
Week 7 midterm; explain the dialectic of lordship and bondage.
Compare Schopenhauer's and Marx's breaks with Hegel.
Explain the pragmatic maxim with three examples.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Kant and after: write a 2,500-word paper that reconstructs one argument from the Critique of Pure Reason (the transcendental deduction, the second analogy or the refutation of idealism), presents one nineteenth-century philosopher's response to it, and evaluates whether the response succeeds.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
